questions.q: A uniform cylindrical rod of length $L$ and radius r, is made from a material whose Young’s modulus of Elasticity equals $Y .$ When this rod is heated by temperature T and simultaneously subjected to a net longutudinal compressional force F, its length remains unchanged. The coefficient of volume expansion, of the material of the rod, is (nearly) equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Stress $= \dfrac{F}{A}$
$Y\left(\alphaT\right) = \dfrac{F}{A}$
$\alpha = \dfrac{F}{A\left(YT\right)}$
$\gamma = 3\alpha = \dfrac{3F}{AYT}$
$\gamma = \dfrac{3F}{\pir^{2}YT}$

questions.q: A cylinder of fixed capacity of $44 . 8$~litres contains helium gas at standard temperature and pressure. The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of gas in the cylinder by $20 . 0 ° C$ will be (Given gas constant $R = 8 . 3JK^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At STP& volume occupied by one mole of a gas is $22 . 4L$. Therefore, number of moles are, $n = \dfrac{44 . 8}{22 . 4} = 2mol$.

The process is isochoric process as the volume of the cylinder remains fixed and~helium is a monatomic gas. Therefore, amount of heat needed will be,

$Q = n Cv \Delta T = \left(2\right)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}R\right)\left(20\right) = 3 \times 8 . 3 \times 20 = 498J$

questions.q: Two identical metal wires of thermal conductivities ${K}_{1}$ and ${K}_{2}$ respectively are connected in series. The effective thermal conductivity of the combination is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${R}_{eff} = \dfrac{l}{{K}_{1}A} + \dfrac{l}{{K}_{2}A} = \dfrac{2l}{{K}_{eq}A}$

${K}_{eq} = \dfrac{2{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}}$

questions.q: A thermometer graduated according to a linear scale reads a value $x_{0}$ when in contact with boiling water, and $x_{0} / 3$ when in contact with ice. What is the temperature of an object in ${ }^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$, if this thermometer in the contact with the object reads $x_{0} / 2 ?$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let required temperature $=\mathrmT^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrmT^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{6}\ \text{ and } \left(\mathrm{x}_{0}-\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{3}\right)=\left(100-0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}\right)\Rightarrow \frac{2 \mathrm{x}_{0}}{3}=100 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_{0}=\frac{300}{2}\Rightarrow \mathrmT^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{0}}{6}=\frac{150}{6}=25^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$

questions.q: When the temperature of a metal wire is increased from& $0 º Cto10 º C$, its length increases by~$0 . 02 %$.The percentage change in its mass density will be closed to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\Deltaℓ = ℓ\alpha\Deltat$
$\alpha = \dfrac{\Deltaℓ}{ℓ\Delta T} = \dfrac{0 . 02}{100 \times 10}; \alpha = 2 \times {10}^{- 5}$
$\gamma = 3\alpha = 6 \times {10}^{- 5}$
$\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = \gamma \times \Delta T; \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100 = \left(6 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 10 \times 100\right) = 6 \times {10}^{- 2}$
Volume increase by~$0 . 06 %$ therefore density decrease by $0 . 06 %$

questions.q: An amount of ice of mass $10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg}$ and temperature $-10^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ is transformed to vapour of temperature $110^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ by applying heat. The total amount of work required for this conversion is, (Take, specific heat of ice $=2100 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, specific heat of water $=4180 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, specific heat of steam $=1920 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, Latent heat of ice $=3.35 \times 10^5 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1}$ and Latent heat of steam $=2.25 \times 10^6\mathrm{Jkg}^{-1}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_1=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{S}_1 \times \Delta \mathrm{T}=10^{-3} \times 2100 \times 10=21 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_2=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{f}}=10^{-3} \times 3.35 \times 10^5=335 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_3=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{w}} \times \Delta \mathrm{T}=10^{-3} \times 4180 \times 100=418 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_4=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{v}}=10^{-3} \times 2.25 \times 10^6=2250 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_5=\mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{v}} \times \Delta \mathrm{T}=10^{-3} \times 1920 \times 10=19.2 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{net}}=3043.2 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Resistance of the wire is measured as $2Ω$~and $3Ω$ at $10 ° C$ and $30 ° C$ respectively. Temperature coefficient of resistance of the material of the wire is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resistance of a material is related to temperature by expression& $R = {R}_{0} \left(1 + \alpha\Delta T\right)$

Here, at~$10 ° C$, we have $2 = {R}_{0} \left(1 + 10\alpha\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

And at~$30 ° C$, we have~$3 = {R}_{0} \left($1 + $30\alpha\right) . . .\left($ii\right)$

From equation~ \left($i\right)$,~${R}_{0} = 2 \left($1 + $10\alpha\right)

Putting this value in equation~\left($ii\right)$,~

$3 = \dfrac{2}{1 + 10\alpha} \left($1 + 30\alpha\right)⇒ 3 + 30\alpha =2 + 60\alpha$

$⇒ 1 = 30\alpha$

Hence, temperature coefficient of the material of wire is~$\alpha = $\dfrac{1}{30} =$0 . 033 ° C^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: $1$ kg of water at $100 ° C$ is converted into steam at $100 ° C$ by boiling at atmospheric pressure. The volume of water changes from $1 . 00 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$~as a liquid to $1 . 671m^{3}$~as steam. The change in internal energy of the system during the process will be (Given latent heat of vaporisation $= 2257kJ / kg$, Atmospheric pressure  \left= 1 \times {10}^{5}Pa\right)$$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work to be done& in the process is given by

$\begin{cases}dW & = & PdV \\ = & 1 \times {10}^{5}Pa \times ( 1 . 671 - 0 . 001 ) m^{3} \\ = & 1 . 670 \times {10}^{5}J\end{cases}$

The change in heat energy during the vaporisation process can be calculated as follows-

$\begin{cases}\Delta{Q}_{supplied } & = & 2257 \times 1 \times {10}^{3}J \\ = & 22 . 57 \times {10}^{5}J\end{cases}$

Hence, the change in internal energy in the process is given by

$\begin{cases}\Delta U & = & \Delta{Q}_{supplied} - \Delta W \\ = & ( 22 . 57 - 1 . 67 ) \times {10}^{5}J \\ = & 20 . 9 \times {10}^{5}J \\ = & 2090kJ\end{cases}$

questions.q: Each side of a box made of metal sheet in cubic shape is $a$~at room temperature $T$, the coefficient of linear expansion of the metal sheet is $\alpha$.~The metal sheet is heated uniformly, by a small temperature $\Delta T$, so that its new temperature is $T + \Delta T$. Calculate the increase in the volume of the metal box.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\Delta V = V\gamma\Delta T$

$\Delta V = 3a^{3}\alpha\Delta T$

questions.q:
A gun fires a lead bullet of temperature 300 K into a wooden block. The bullet having melting temperature of 600 K penetrates into the block and melts down. If the total heat required for the process is 625 J , then the mass of the bullet is $\qquad$ grams.
(Latent heat of fusion of lead $=2.5 \times 10^4 \mathrm{JKg}^{-1}$ and specific heat capacity of lead $=125 \mathrm{JKg}^{-1}  \left.\mathrmK^{-1}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 625=\mathrm{ms} \Delta \mathrm{T}+\mathrm{mL} \\ & 625=\mathrm{m}\left[125 \times 300+2.5 \times 10^4\right] \\ & 625=\mathrm{m}[37500+25000] \\ & 625=\mathrm{m}[62500] \\ & \mathrm{m}=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{M}=10 \text { grams }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two rods $A$ and $B$ of identical dimensions are at temperature $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$. If $\mathrm{A}$ is heated upto $180^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ upto $\mathrmT^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C},$ then the new lengths are the same. If the ratio of the coefficients of linear expansion of $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ is $4: 3,$ then the value of $T$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Change in length in both rods are same i.e. $\Delta \ell_{1}=\Delta \ell_{2}\ell \alpha_{1} \Delta \theta_{1}=\ell \alpha_{2} \Delta \theta_{2}$\begin{array}{l} \frac{\alpha_{1}}{\alpha_{2}}=\frac{\Delta \theta_{2}}{\Delta \theta_{1}} \quad\left[\because \frac{\alpha_{1}}{\alpha_{2}}=\frac{4}{3}\right] \\ \frac{4}{3}=\frac{\theta-30}{180-30} \end{array}$ $\theta=230^{\circ} \mathrm{C}

questions.q: A heat source at $T = {10}^{3}K$ is connected to another heat reservoir at $T = {10}^{2}K$ by a copper slab which is $1m$ thick. Given that the thermal conductivity of copper is $0 .1 WK^{- 1}m^{- 1}$, the energy flux through it in the steady-state is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Temperature of heat source,& ${T}_{H} = {10}^{3}K$,

Temperature of heat reservoir,~${T}_{L} = {10}^{2}K$,

Conductivity of copper~$K = 0 . 1WK^{- 1}m^{- 1}$

From the equation of steady-state heat flow,

$\dfrac{d Q}{d t} = \dfrac{KA ∆ T}{L}$

Heat energy flux~can be defined as the rate of heat energy transfer through a given surface.

$\dfrac{1}{A}\left(\dfrac{d Q}{d t}\right) = K \times \dfrac{1000 - 100}{1} = 90Wm^{- 2}$

questions.q: A solid metallic cube having total surface area $24m^{2}$ is uniformly heated. If its temperature is increased by $10 ° C$, calculate the increase in volume of the cube. (Given $\alpha = 5 . 0 \times {10}^{- 4}{C ∘}^{- 1}$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total surface area of a cube is& $6a^{2} = 24m^{2}⇒ a^{2} = 4$~$⇒ a = 2m$

Volume of a cube~$V = a^{3} = 8m^{3}$

Change in volume is given by,~

$\Delta V = {V}_{0}\gamma\Delta T$,~where $\gamma = 3\alpha$

$\Delta V = \left[8\right] \times \left[1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}\right] \times \left[10\right]m^{3}⇒ \Delta V = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{5}{cm}^{3}$

questions.q: Two metallic blocks ${M}_{1}$ and ${M}_{2}$ of same area of cross-section are connected to each other (as shown in figure). If the thermal conductivity of ${M}_{2}$ is $K$ then the thermal conductivity of ${M}_{1}$ will be : [Assume steady state heat conduction]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let thermal conductivity of& ${M}_{1}$~be~$K '$.

Using heat current relation for steady state conduction,

$\dfrac{K ' A\left(100 - 80\right)}{16} = \dfrac{KA\left(80 - 0\right)}{8}$

$⇒ \dfrac{K ' \times 20}{16} = \dfrac{K \times 80}{8} ⇒ K ' = 8K$

questions.q: Two identical beakers $A$ and $B$ contain equal volumes of two different liquids at $60 ° C$ each and left to cool down. Liquid in $A$ has density of $8 \times {10}^{2}kgm^{- 3}$ and specific heat of $2000Jkg^{- 1}K^{- 1}$ while the liquid in $B$ has density ${10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$ and specific heat of $4000Jkg^{- 1}K^{- 1}$. Which of the following best describes their temperature versus time graph schematically? (assume the emissivity of both the beakers to be the same)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Newton's law of cooling,
Rate of cooling: \left(- \dfrac{dT}{dt}\right) = \dfrac{4\sigmaeA{T}_{0}^{3}\left(T - {T}_{0}\right)}{ms}∝ \dfrac{1}{ms}$
$∴ {ρ}_{A} < {ρ}_{B}$
${m}_{A} < {m}_{B}$
And ${s}_{A} < {s}_{B}$
${m}_{A}{s}_{A} < {m}_{B}{s}_{B}$
At $t = 0, {\left(- \dfrac{dT}{dt}\right)}_{A} > {\left(- \dfrac{dT}{dt}\right)}_{B}$
Initially, the rate of cooling for $A$ will be higher than $B$ and temperature $( T )$ vs time $( t )$ graph will be a curve.$

questions.q:
At what temperature a gold ring of diameter $6 . 230cm$ be heated so that it can be fitted on a wooden bangle of diameter $6 . 241cm$? Both the diameters have been measured at room temperature \left(27 ° C\right)$.
(Given: coefficient of linear thermal expansion of gold ${α}_{L} = 1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 5}K^{- 1}$)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
To fit gold ring of diameter $5 . 230cm$ over wooden bangle of diameter $6 . 241cm$, gold ring expansion is required.

So,~$l = {l}_{0} \left[1 + \alpha\Delta T\right]$

$⇒ 6 . 241 = 6 . 230 \left[1 + 1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 5} \left(T - 27\right)\right]$

$⇒ $\dfrac{6 . 241}{6 . 230} -$1 = 1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 5} \left(T - 27\right)$

$⇒ T = 152 . 7 ° C

$

questions.q: A cylinder of radius $R$ is surrounded by a cylindrical shell of inner radius $R$ and outer radius $2R$. The thermal conductivity of the material of the inner cylinder is ${K}_{1}$ and that of the outer cylinder is ${K}_{2}$.& Assuming no loss of heat, the effective thermal conductivity of the system for heat flowing along the& length of the cylinder is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

Let ${q}_{1}$ and ${q}_{2}$ be the rate of flow of heat through inner part from outer part respecting net flow of heat


$q = {q}_{1} + {q}_{2}$

$= \dfrac{{K}_{1}\piR^{2}}{l} . \Delta T + \dfrac{{K}_{2} . \pi\left[{\left(2R\right)}^{2} - R^{2}\right]}{l} . \Delta T$

$= \dfrac{\piR^{2}}{l}\Delta T \left({K}_{1} +3{K}_{2}\right)$

If the cylinder is replaced by a single material of thermal conductivity $K$ then

$q = $\dfrac{K . {\left(2R\right)}^{2}}{l} . \Delta$T$

On comparison,

$K = \dfrac{{K}_{1} + 3{K}_{2}}{4}.$

$

questions.q: According to law of equipartition of energy the molar specific heat of a diatomic gas at constant volume where the molecule has one additional vibrational mode is :-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A diatomic gas has 5 degrees of freedom apart from vibrational degree of freedom. For each additional vibrational mode, degree of freedom is increased by $2$. So new degree of freedom,

$f = 5 + 2 = 7$

Therefore, we require~molar specific heat capacity at constant volume, which is given by

${C}_{v} = \dfrac{f}{2}R = \dfrac{7}{2}R$

questions.q: A hole is drilled in a metal sheet. At $27 ° C$, the diameter of hole is $5$ cm. When the sheet is heated to $177 ° C$, the change in the diameter of hole is $d \times {10}^{- 3}cm$ . The value of $d$ will be _____, if coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is $1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 5} / C ∘$&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Expansion of hole will be similar to that of an imaginary disc.

Let diameter be& ${d}_{0}$~at $27 ° C$~and $d^{'}$~at $177 ° C$. Therefore, we can write

$d^{'} = {d}_{0} \left(1 + \alpha\Delta T\right)$

Therefore, change in diameter will be

$⇒ d^{'} - {d}_{0} = \left(5\right)\times \left(1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 5}\right) \times \left(177 - 27\right)$

$= 12 \times {10}^{- 3}cm$

Hence, required value of~$d = 12$.

questions.q:
Three containers ${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ have water at different temperatures. The table below shows the final temperature $T$ when different amounts of water (given in liters) are taken from each container and mixed (assume no loss of heat during the process)




































${C}_{1}$ ${C}_{2}$ ${C}_{3}$ $T$
$1l$ $2l$ $- -$ ${60}^{o}C$
$- -$ $1l$ $2l$ ${30}^{o}C$
$2l$ $- -$ $1l$ ${60}^{o}C$
$1l$ $1l$ $1l$ $\theta$


The value of $\theta$ (in ${}^{o}C$ to the nearest integer) is___________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& ${θ}_{1}$,~${θ}_{2}$~and~${θ}_{3}$~be the~temperatures of water in three containers.

$1{θ}_{1} + 2{θ}_{2} + 0{θ}_{3} = \left(1 + 2\right)60$
${\theta}_{1} + 2{\theta}_{2} = 180$ …. (1)
$0 \times {\theta}_{1} + 1 \times {\theta}_{2} + 2 \times {\theta}_{3} = \left(1 + 2\right)30$
${\theta}_{2} + 2{\theta}_{3} = 90$ …… (2)
$2 \times {\theta}_{1} + 0 \times {\theta}_{2} + 1 \times {\theta}_{3} = \left(2 + 1\right)60$
$2{\theta}_{1} + {\theta}_{3} = 180$ …. (3)
and ${\theta}_{1} + {\theta}_{2} + {\theta}_{3} = \left(1 + 1 + 1\right)\theta$
from (1)+(2)+(3)
$3{θ}_{1} + 3{θ}_{2} + 3{θ}_{3} = 450 ⟹ {θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} + {θ}_{3} = 150$
from (4) equation $150 = 3\theta ⟹ \theta = 50 ° C$

questions.q:
A unit scale is to be prepared whose length does not change with temperature and remains $20$ cm, using a bimetallic strip made of brass and iron each of different length. The length of both components would change in such a way that difference between their lengths remains constant. If length of brass is $40$ cm and length of iron will be _____~$cm$.

\left({α}_{iron} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 5}K^{- 1}\right and {α}_{brass} = 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}K^{- 1})$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Linear expansion of solid with temperature is given by& ${L}_{f} = {L}_{0} \left(1 + \alpha∆ T\right)$

Here,~${l}_{B}\left(1 + {α}_{B}\Delta T\right) - {l}_{i}\left(1 + {α}_{i}\Delta T\right) = {l}_{B} - {l}_{i}$

$⇒ {α}_{B}{l}_{B} = {l}_{i}{α}_{i}$

$⇒ 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5} \times40 = {l}_{i} \times1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 5}$

$⇒ {l}_{i} = $\dfrac{1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 40}{1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{3 \times 40}{2} =$60$

$⇒ {l}_{i} = 60cm

$

questions.q:
A water heater of power $2000W$~is used to heat water. The specific heat capacity of water is $4200J{kg}^{- 1}K^{- 1}$. The efficiency of heater is $70 %$. Time required to heat $2$ kg of water from $10 ° C$~to $60 ° C$~is _____~$s$.

(Assume that the specific heat capacity of water remains constant over the temperature range of the water).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat provided to water will be responsible for increase in temperature. Therefore, we can write

$η \times P \times t = M \times s \times \Delta T$

Now,~$η = \dfrac{70}{100} = 0 . 7$~and $\text{energy} = \text{power} \times \text{time}$.

Therefore,

$t = \dfrac{2 \times 4200 \times \left(60 ° - 10 °\right)}{0 . 7 \times 2000}s = 300s$
